voyage.content: Old furniture store converted to the latest wine-bar in SoMa.

voyage.name: Hotel Utah Saloon
voyage.content: Popular brewery with frequent live music.

voyage.name: Press Club
voyage.content: This bar focuses on wine, with some of the finest from the nearby Wine Country. Sneak a peek at the wine cellar, and don't be surprised if you're super critical of the next glass of wine you drain outside the Press Club. Be prepared, however, to put a dent in your credit card or wallet by the end of the night.
Lines all night outside during the weekend. A twenty-something meat market.

voyage.name: The Cat Club
voyage.content: Thursday is 80s night where you're guaranteed to hear at least one Madonna song throughout the night.

voyage.name: DNA Lounge
voyage.price: There is usually a cover between $3 and $25 (for the bands)
voyage.content: The DNA Lounge is a 2-story club which often caters to the geekier "digerati" crowd. One of the founders is Jamie Zawinski, a former Netscape superstar and Internet nabob. Events feature themed electronica dance nights (Industrial, Techno, Trance, etc.) and live bands. Open on Christmas for goth night.

voyage.name: The End Up
voyage.content: An SF institution. Essentially doesn't close on the weekend, and thus where people 'end up'. Great old school SF house music. Unexpected outdoor patio/waterfall space to chill.

voyage.name: Mezzanine
voyage.content: Where all the shirtless buff gay boys go. Great sound system. If you like cheesy techno and disco diva wailing music, this is the place.

voyage.name: The Stud
voyage.content: Fun semi-dingy club. Don't miss Trannyshack, Tuesdays at midnight. Very worth the sleep deprivation at work the next day. A collectively owned queer bar.

voyage.name: Mosser Hotel
voyage.content: Nice, clean hotel with small rooms but a great location.

voyage.name: Pickwick Hotel
voyage.content: A historic hotel with very nice guestrooms and flexible meeting space.

voyage.name: Hotel Whitcomb
voyage.content: This is a 460 room historic boutique hotel. An elegant, opulent building, it was first used as a temporary city hall after the 1906 earthquake. Italian marble, Austrian chandeliers, and a short walk to the Symphony/Opera and the Asian Art Museum. It also has a piano bar/wine bar.

voyage.name: The Clancy
voyage.content: A Marriot with all the amenities that generally come with it.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Hotel
voyage.content: Very high-end hotel. Beautiful art collection, and extensive sports club with fitness facilities and spa.

voyage.name: Harbor Court Hotel
voyage.content: A waterfront boutique hotel on the Embarcadero, across from the San Francisco Ferry Building, with views onto San Francisco Bay.

voyage.name: Hotel Griffon
voyage.content: A comparatively smaller hotel with small but very comfy rooms and good service.

voyage.name: InterContinental Hotel
voyage.content: A translucent cool-blue tower that doubles as a city landmark.

voyage.name: Marriott Marquis
voyage.content: Convention center hotel across the street from the Moscone Center.

voyage.name: The Palace Hotel
voyage.content: Established in 1875, the Palace has 552 guest rooms. In 1945, the official banquet honoring the opening session of the United Nations was held in The Garden Court at The Palace. The Garden Court is also the place to go to for traditional afternoon tea, but naturally with a hefty price tag.

voyage.name: St. Regis Hotel
voyage.content: A historic and very upscale hotel with a spa, butler service, and on-site restaurant.

voyage.name: W Hotel
voyage.content: Another major convention center hotel, with lots of amenities and very nice rooms.

voyage.name: Alamo Square Park
voyage.content: This park is best known for the famous Painted Ladies row of Victorian houses on its east side along Steiner Street, which is often the subject of many a San Francisco postcard. There are also many other pretty Victorians encircling the lovely park. The 6-Hayes bus route goes along its south side, the 5-Fulton bus passes by a block north of the park, or if you enjoy walking and don't mind modest grades you can get th

voyage.name: Japantown
voyage.content: Peace Plaza and shopping mall; Ruth Asawa's incredible wrought and cast bronze origami fountains on the Nihonmachi Pedestrian Mall. At the center entrance to the Japan Center is a five-tiered Peace Pagoda, it was designed by world-famous Japanese architect Yoshiro Taniguchi. The Center opened in 1968.

voyage.name: The Panhandle
voyage.address: (between Fell and Oak, Steiner and Baker streets)
voyage.content: This long narrow park is the main entrance to Golden Gate Park, which goes for another 40+ blocks to the west (and the Pacific Ocean). The Panhandle also includes the most famous bicycle route in the city, the Wiggle, which follows the easy grades of a former creekbed to connect Market Street with the Fillmore, Haight, Golden Gate Park and the Avenues. You'll find a playground, basketball courts, dog walking, weekend

voyage.name: Fillmore Auditorium
voyage.content: Hosts concerts and contemporary bands.

voyage.name: Kabuki Springs & Spa
voyage.content: Traditional Japanese-style onsen with full spa services. Communal baths are co-ed only one day per week, see calendar for details.

voyage.name: University of San Francisco Dons
voyage.price: General admission for any game: $7-10 adults, $5-7 seniors, $3-5 children
voyage.content: Various college sports including baseball, basketball, soccer and volleyball.

voyage.name: Cherry Blossom Festival
voyage.content: In Japantown in the spring since 1967, this popular festival includes a parade from the Civic Center to the Japantown mall area, a street fair, music and a lot to do. Great event to take kids to.

voyage.name: Juneteenth Festival
voyage.content: San Francisco joins towns and cities across the U.S. in celebrating the arrival of the news of Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation on June 19, 1863. Juneteenth is a celebration of African-American culture as well as a celebration of freedom from slavery and remembrance of what it is to be free.

voyage.name: Fillmore Street Jazz Festival
voyage.content: A jazz festival with several music stages and a street arts fair to Fillmore Street between Jackson and Eddy.

voyage.name: Nihonmachi Street Fair
voyage.content: This street fair has been celebrating San Francisco's Asian cultures and raising funds for community organizations since 1973.

voyage.name: Soko Hardware
voyage.content: Has everything from copper rain chains and iron cabinetry findings, fine woodworking tools to bulk nails, porcelain to everyday kitchenware; just what you want in a longstanding hardware store.

voyage.name: Maido Stationery
voyage.content: Has a huge collection of washii decorative papers that is only surpassed by their incredible collection of pens, stationery and gift items.

voyage.name: Kinokuniya Bookstore
voyage.content: If you're into Japanese books, magazines, or comic books (otherwise known as manga), then this is your place to be. The only San Francisco branch of the famous Japanese chain, Kinokuniya carries thousands of titles, including dozens in English. So a crash course in Japanese is not essential to shop here.

voyage.name: Forest Books
voyage.content: A moderately sized bookstore selling new and mostly used books.

voyage.name: Nijiya Market
voyage.content: This extensive Japanese grocery store has remarkably good takeout sushi, which can be pleasantly eaten in either of the plazas that are part of Japantown.

voyage.name: Absinthe
voyage.content: Restyles the rustic foods of southern France into sleek urban classics. Wonderful (expensive) cocktails based on 100-year old recipes. Not the cheapest place in town, but affordable and the quality of the food is an excellent value. A pretty, white-tablecloth setting and excellent service make this a lovely lunch spot. Avoid weekend evenings before 8PM, when crowds from the nearby theater district can mean a wait. An

voyage.name: On the Bridge
voyage.content: This ultra-cute little eatery, on the bridge connecting the Kintetsu and Kinokuniya Buildings, specializes in an intriguing Euro-Japanese and Indo-Japanese hybrid cuisine called yoshoku, which has been popular in Japan for more than 100 years. Japanese 'pastas' and curried rice plates take on unexpected but delightful flavors.

voyage.name: SPQR
voyage.hours: Mon-Tue 11:30AM-2:30PM and 5PM-10PM, Wed-Thu 5PM-10PM, Fri 5PM-11PM, Sat 11:30AM-11PM, Sun 11:30AM-10PM
voyage.content: Beautiful European stylized restaurant with a great menu of Italian cuisine and wine, serving walk-ins only - keeping the clientèle local and less stuffy than reservation only dinning.

voyage.name: Suppenküche
voyage.content: For casual German food and service, beer -- of course -- served at shared tables.

voyage.name: Mel's Drive-In
voyage.content: This all day, late night diner is a classic bit of Americana, full of shiny stainless steel walls and counters. It's covered in American Graffiti movie posters and outtake photos, since part of the film was shot in this small chain's Lombard St. diner. Good solid comfort food, free parking, with good desserts and ice cream treats. A jukebox control at every table, sucking down your quarters to hear hits from the 1950

voyage.name: Biergarten
voyage.content: Do not expect a picturesque Bavarian scene but you will find familiar beer and food.

voyage.name: Boom Boom Room
voyage.content: A super fun bar with live blues, rock and funk bands.

voyage.name: Harry's Bar
voyage.content: Good neighborhood bar in Pacific Heights with a casual atmosphere. Popular with local professionals.

voyage.name: Hayes Valley Inn
voyage.content: European Style. Extremely cute, homey, and comfortable.

voyage.name: Hotel Kabuki
voyage.content: A Japanese-style hotel with a calm ambiance.

voyage.name: Queen Anne Hotel
voyage.content: The Queen Anne provides a real San Francisco experience, being an 1890 Victorian Hotel between Pacific Heights and the Civic Center, and near Japantown. Some rooms have fireplaces, and afternoon tea is served daily.

voyage.name: Inn At The Opera
voyage.content: This hotel has 29 guestrooms and 18 suites which are individually decorated. It is situated in an excellent location.
